stories.headline: Twenty-one students faint after experiencing shortness of breath at school in Myanmar YANGON: A total of 21 students experienced shortness of breath and fainted at No. 1 Basic Education High School in Dawei, Tanintharyi Region, on June 26, accord
stories.summary: Twenty-one students at No. 1 Basic Education High School in Dawei, Tanintharyi Region, Myanmar, experienced shortness of breath and fainted on June 26. The incident occurred at the school, with all 21 students reportedly suffering from similar symptoms. The cause of the shortness of breath and fainting has not been specified. The students were likely given medical attention, although the current status of their health is unknown. The incident is an isolated event, but it raises concerns about the health and safety of students in Myanmar's schools. Further investigation is needed to determine the cause of the incident and prevent similar occurrences in the future. The school and local authorities have not released a statement on the incident, leaving many questions unanswered.

stories.headline: Will face hell: Iran's stark warning to US, Gulf nations amid escalating attacks Iran launched missile and drone strikes on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain after fresh American attacks on Iranian targets. As tensions surged despite a
stories.summary: Iran launched missile and drone strikes on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for fresh American attacks on Iranian targets. The strikes come after the US attacked Iranian ports and islands in the Strait of Hormuz over the downing of a helicopter. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for the joint missile and drone operations. The US has warned Iran that it could "cease to exist" if Washington is forced to escalate its military response. Kuwait and Bahrain have activated their air defenses, and the UN has warned of a possible return to full-scale war in the Middle East. The attacks have raised tensions despite a fragile ceasefire, with the US and Iran engaging in a series of escalating attacks and warnings. The situation remains volatile, with the potential for further conflict.

stories.headline: Explosions, 90-minute gun battle: How Karachi terror attack that killed 4 Pakistani soldiers unfolded Terrorists stormed the Sindh Rangers compound after an explosives-laden vehicle rammed into the building, breaching the premises before attackers opened fire |
stories.summary: Terrorists stormed the Sindh Rangers compound in Karachi's Gulistan-i-Jauhar neighbourhood after an explosives-laden vehicle rammed into the building, breaching the premises. The attackers, believed to be from Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a splinter faction of the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban, then opened fire on the troops. A 90-minute gun battle ensued, resulting in the deaths of four Pakistani soldiers. The attack is part of the ongoing insurgency in northwest Pakistan, which has been fought since 2004. The Pakistani Taliban is suspected to be involved in the attack, which has raised concerns about the security of the city. The incident highlights the ongoing threat of terrorism in the region and the challenges faced by security forces in combating it. The attack on the Sindh Rangers compound is a significant incident in the ongoing conflict.

stories.headline: Vietnam police bust transnational online fraud ring, arrest 12 suspects NINH BINH, Vietnam: Police in the northern province of Ninh Binh have dismantled a transnational cyber fraud ring accused of swindling more than VND250 billion
stories.summary: Police in Vietnam's northern province of Ninh Binh have dismantled a transnational cyber fraud ring, arresting 12 suspects. The ring is accused of swindling over VND250 billion (approximately $9.6 million) from around 500 victims across Vietnam. The fraud ring, which was based in Cambodia, allegedly deceived victims through online means. The police operation resulted in the arrest of 12 suspects and the dismantling of the transnational network. The total amount stolen is estimated to be over VND250 billion, with victims spread across the country. The arrest and dismantling of the ring is a significant crackdown on cyber fraud in Vietnam, with authorities continuing to investigate and take action against similar transnational crime networks. The operation highlights the ongoing efforts of Vietnamese law enforcement to combat online fraud and protect citizens from financial crimes.

stories.headline: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Release Date: Now Confirmed
stories.summary: Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 release date is confirmed as July 22, 2026, in London. The device has cleared FCC certification, indicating a US launch is on track for the same date. Leaks reveal the phone will come in various colors and storage tiers. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is expected to feature a 6.5-inch cover screen with Gorilla Glass Ceramic 2 and an 8-inch inner display, with no upgrades to display sizes. The device will be unveiled at Galaxy Unpacked 2026, alongside the Galaxy Z Flip 8 and Watch 9. Additional features, such as Gemini AI, are also expected to be introduced. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is rumored to offer one of the sharpest displays in foldable smartphones, with the US launch confirmed for July 22.

stories.headline: Amazon Prime Day 2026 New Launches Revealed: Samsung Galaxy M47, OnePlus N6, boAt Nirvana Eutopia, and More
stories.summary: Amazon Prime Day 2026 will feature new launches, including the Samsung Galaxy M47 5G, which packs a 50MP OIS camera and a 6,000mAh battery with 45W fast charging. OnePlus will introduce the N6, its first new series since the Nord in 2020. Other products include the boAt Nirvana Eutopia and devices from Redmi, iQOO, HP, Asus, and Lenovo. Over 500 new products will be available during Prime Day, which ran from June 23 to June 26, but new launches will continue, with Samsung's Galaxy M47 launching on June 29. The Galaxy M47 will be an Amazon special, powered by a Snapdragon chipset. These new launches will be available on Amazon India, offering customers a range of new products to choose from. The Samsung Galaxy M47 and other devices will be available starting June 29.

stories.headline: From casual hobby to luxury investment: memory costs hit PC gaming hard
stories.summary: The PC gaming industry is facing significant price increases due to a memory shortage, driven by the artificial intelligence boom. DDR5 memory prices have doubled since September, with premium kits rising by 138% in two months. The shortage has led to RAM and SSD prices soaring, making PC gaming increasingly expensive. This shift is attributed to chipmakers prioritizing lucrative enterprise contracts over consumer supply, driven by AI's high demand for memory. As a result, building a gaming rig has become more costly, with prices hitting companies and individuals without strong bargaining power the hardest. The price hikes are affecting every layer of the hobby, pushing PC gaming into luxury territory and raising questions about the value of the latest developments.

stories.headline: ThinkPad X1 2-in-1 Gen 11 review: Most compelling convertible yet from Lenovo
stories.summary: Lenovo has revamped its ThinkPad X1 lineup, including the ThinkPad X1 2-in-1 Gen 11, a 14.0-inch business convertible laptop with a Windows operating system. The new model features Intel Core Ultra X9 CPUs, a more repairable design, and a new place for the pen to stay. The ThinkPad X1 2-in-1 Gen 11 has a starting weight of 1.18 kg, decreased from the previous generation's 1.22 kg. It will launch in March 2026 with a starting price of $2,149. The laptop is suitable for students and professionals who need a premium, long-lasting convertible for demanding tasks, remote collaboration, and creative projects. The ThinkPad X1 2-in-1 Gen 11 Aura Edition is considered one of the strongest contenders in its class for 2026, offering a pen and touch experience with improved usability and design.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi ascends to top spot of all time, hits No. 19 with splendid free kick
stories.summary: Lionel Messi has become the all-time leading scorer in the World Cup, achieving his 19th career goal in the tournament. He scored his 17th and 18th goals during Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria. Messi then added his 19th goal against Jordan with a sublime free kick from outside the box in the 80th minute. This strike was his sixth goal of the tournament, extending his lead in the Golden Boot race. The goal broke his own record, solidifying his position as the top men's or women's World Cup scorer. Messi's achievement comes after his two goals against Austria, which initially propelled him to the top spot. His record-breaking goal against Jordan has further cemented his status as one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.

stories.headline: Scans confirm ACL injury and season over for Manly Sea Eagles’ Luke Brooks
stories.summary: Manly Sea Eagles playmaker Luke Brooks' season is over after scans confirmed an ACL rupture. The injury occurred during a game at Brookvale Oval on Saturday night against Melbourne. Brooks suffered the injury in the first half but continued playing for 15 minutes before being forced to leave the game at halftime. The ACL rupture was initially suspected, and scans have since confirmed the diagnosis. This marks a significant setback for the experienced playmaker, ending his season prematurely. The news comes as another NRL player, Wests Tigers centre Taylan May, also faces a season-ending injury with a third dislocated shoulder. Brooks' courage in playing on with the injury has been noted, but ultimately, the severity of the injury has brought his season to an early close.

stories.headline: Portugal coach: 'Childish' to compare Ronaldo's needs to Messi's
stories.summary: Portugal coach Roberto Martinez has defended Cristiano Ronaldo's workload at the 2026 World Cup, dismissing comparisons to Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland. Ronaldo played a full 90 minutes in Portugal's 0-0 draw against Colombia, sparking suggestions he should be rested like other top players. Martinez labeled such comparisons as "childish," insisting Ronaldo remains capable of playing every minute of the tournament. The 41-year-old captain has played continuously for Portugal, while other top teams have rested their star players, including Messi and Haaland. Martinez's decision to keep Ronaldo on the field has raised questions, but the coach is confident in his captain's abilities to perform at a high level throughout the World Cup. Portugal finished second in Group K after the draw with Colombia.

stories.headline: NRL world rallies around Luke Brooks after shattering news as Manly teammate learns fate Sea Eagles coach Kieran Foran discussed the 'devastating' situation after the win
stories.summary: Luke Brooks' NRL season has been cut short due to a ruptured ACL, suffered during Manly's win over Melbourne. The injury occurred at Brookvale Oval on Saturday night, with Brooks spotted leaving the field with ice on his knee. Manly coach Kieran Foran described the situation as "devastating" and confirmed that scans had confirmed the ACL rupture. The Sea Eagles are rallying around Brooks, with Foran stating that the team is "all shattered" for him. In a separate development, teammate Joey Walsh was not charged, providing some positive news for the club. Brooks' injury is a significant blow, ruling him out for the remainder of the season. The Sea Eagles will now need to adjust their lineup to compensate for the loss of their experienced playmaker.

stories.headline: Delhi YouTuber Crashed Into Women Riders, Filmed Them For Views, Arrested
stories.summary: Delhi Police have arrested 32-year-old YouTuber Gurman Singh, known as "Road Safety Wala," for allegedly targeting women riders and minor girls by deliberately crashing into their two-wheelers. Singh would then film the encounters, pretending the collisions were accidents, and post the videos online for views and monetization. The YouTuber's actions were reportedly intended to harass and stalk the victims, with the footage used as content for his channel. The arrest was made after complaints were filed against Singh, who has been accused of turning harassment into online content. The Delhi Police have taken action against the YouTuber for his alleged crimes, which include stalking, harassment, and deliberately causing accidents for the purpose of creating video content.

stories.headline: MEA warns Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims against travelling without China permits and visas
stories.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has warned Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims against traveling without obtaining necessary permits and visas from China. The caution comes as many devotees have faced permit denials, border delays, and uncertainty despite completing required formalities. The MEA advised pilgrims not to commence their journey without securing all necessary documents, including a Chinese visa from the Embassy of China in New Delhi. This is a requirement for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, a sacred pilgrimage. The warning is aimed at pilgrims planning to travel via private operators, emphasizing the need to arrange all permits and visas before departure to avoid getting stranded. The Embassy of China has confirmed that a Chinese visa is mandatory, contrary to claims of visa-free travel by some local travel agencies. Pilgrims are urged to verify requirements before embarking on their journey.

stories.headline: Cop slaps woman complainant at Delhi hotel, clash ensues; probe ordered
stories.summary: A Delhi Police sub-inspector has been removed from active field duty pending an enquiry after a video showed him slapping a woman during an intervention at a hotel in Adarsh Nagar, northwest Delhi. The incident reportedly took place at a hotel in Panchwati, where a police operation was underway. CCTV footage allegedly shows the sub-inspector slapping two women, sparking controversy. A vigilance enquiry has been ordered into the incident by senior police officer Akanksha Yadav. Counter allegations have been made, and an investigation is underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The video of the incident has been circulating, prompting a probe into the sub-inspector's actions. The enquiry aims to establish the facts and take necessary action against the officer if found guilty of misconduct.

stories.headline: 'Meant to relieve pain': Capsules with rat poison given at Moharram procession in Mumbai; BBA grad from Pune held
stories.summary: Mumbai Police detained a businessman from Pune after seizing 14,900 capsules filled with zinc phosphide during a Muharram procession. The capsules were allegedly distributed with the intent to cause "mass harm". The suspect claimed the capsules were meant to relieve pain. Investigators are examining his travels, finances, and contacts for possible wider links. A major tragedy was averted due to the police's swift action. The incident occurred during a Muharram procession in the city, where the suspect was noticed distributing the capsules. The police have arrested the suspect, a BBA graduate from Pune, and are further investigating the matter. The seized capsules contain zinc phosphide, a toxic substance commonly used as rat poison. The police are working to determine the suspect's motives and potential connections to other individuals or groups.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal to US-Iran war: Top five triggers that may dictate the Indian stock market this week
stories.summary: The Indian stock market is expected to be influenced by several key factors this week. A potential trade deal between India and the US is a major trigger, with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal leading discussions with US trade officials. The ongoing US-Iran conflict and rising crude oil prices may also impact the market, particularly affecting sectors such as auto, cement, metals, and pharma. The RBI MPC meeting is another significant event that could dictate market trends. A delay in signing a trade deal with the US could expose India to higher tariffs under the Section 301 probe, making it an expensive proposition. These factors will be closely watched by investors, with the Sensex and Nifty indices likely to be volatile in response to these developments. Key stocks in affected sectors will be under scrutiny.

stories.headline: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide D-Street action on Monday
stories.summary: The Indian stock market's action on Monday will be influenced by several key factors. These include Federal Bank, YES Bank, and IndusInd Bank share prices, as well as developments related to IDFC First. Global policy sentiment, particularly the Fed's rate cut, will also play a role. Additionally, FII flows and US-India tariff developments are expected to impact the market. Other domestic challenges and economic indicators will also be closely watched. The balance between these factors will determine the direction of the market. Investors will be looking for cues from these developments to make informed decisions. The market's performance will be shaped by a combination of global and domestic factors, making it a closely watched event.

stories.headline: Persistent and Nagarro sign Business Combination Agreement to form the Persistent – Nagarro Group, a global leader in AI-led digital engineering
stories.summary: Persistent Systems and Nagarro have signed a Business Combination Agreement to form the Persistent – Nagarro Group, a global leader in AI-led digital engineering. The deal values the combined entity at $2.9 billion. Persistent Systems aims to acquire Nagarro for €1.1 billion, creating a powerhouse in AI-led digital engineering. The combined group will have a strong presence globally, leveraging the capabilities of both companies. The move is driven by the shared conviction that leading the next decade of AI-led digital engineering requires a strong local presence and capabilities. The formation of the Persistent – Nagarro Group is expected to create a global leader in AI-led digital engineering, with a significant valuation and presence in the industry. The acquisition is a strategic step to enhance the companies' position in the digital engineering market.

stories.headline: Indian markets closed marginally higher on Thursday after a volatile expiry session, with the Sensex rising 109 points to 77,100.47 and the Nifty gaining 34 points
stories.summary: Indian markets closed marginally higher on Thursday after a volatile expiry session. The Sensex rose 109 points to 77,100.47, a 0.14% increase, while the Nifty gained 34 points to 24,056, also a 0.14% increase. Despite giving up intraday gains, the markets were bolstered by strong performances from IndiGo, M&M, and Maruti Suzuki. However, Power Grid shares saw notable declines. The gains were also supported by easing crude oil prices. The Sensex and Nifty had briefly traded at significantly higher levels during the session before settling at their closing points. The marginal increase indicates a stable market performance amidst volatility, with key stocks contributing to the overall gain. The closing points reflect a minor upside, with the Sensex at 77,100.47 and the Nifty at 24,056.

stories.headline: VinFast Viper Electric Scooter Patented In India: Is The Vietnamese EV Giant Preparing Its 2W Entry
stories.summary: VinFast, a Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer, has patented its Viper electric scooter in India, hinting at a potential entry into the country's two-wheeler market. The scooter features a 1.5 kWh fixed battery, allowing it to reach a top speed of 70 km/h and cover a distance of 82 km. This development comes after VinFast announced plans to invest ₹7,000 crore in India to manufacture electric scooters, buses, and expand its EV ecosystem. The company is expected to launch three electric scooters in India, including the Evo 200 and Feliz S. The patent filing suggests that VinFast is preparing to enter India's growing electric scooter segment, which has seen significant growth in recent years. The move is part of VinFast's broader expansion plans in the Indian market.

stories.headline: Fuel prices in Australia are back to pre-war levels. Will it last
stories.summary: Fuel prices in Australia have returned to pre-war levels, providing relief to motorists. The current prices are approximately 40% lower than the peak during the Iran conflict. This decrease comes four months after the conflict began, with petrol prices now lower than before the war started. However, the subdued prices may not last, as regional oil prices have climbed to wartime highs, potentially leading to a spike in fuel prices within days. The oil crisis, initially expected to outlast the end of hostilities, may still impact fuel prices in the future. The current reprieve for Australian motorists may be short-lived, with prices potentially increasing as the conflict continues to affect global oil supply.

stories.headline: Trend Micro Stock And 2 Japanese AI Shares Backed By Real Business Demand
stories.summary: Trend Micro shares rose nearly 12% to 6,100.0 yen in Tokyo trading, making it one of the top performers on the Nikkei 225 index. The index itself surged more than 2% to a record high. Trend Micro's enterprise AI cybersecurity business, TrendAI, delivered 50% year-over-year growth in Vision One ARR, driven by surging demand for AI security. The company has launched two purpose-built business units, TrendAI and TrendLife, to lead enterprise and consumer cybersecurity into the AI era. Trend Micro has partnered with industry leaders like NVIDIA and Anthropic, incorporating the latter's Claude artificial intelligence models. The stock briefly hit a near three-month high of 6,294.0 yen, driven by the positive news and growing demand for AI-related investments. This growth is backed by policy support, corporate spending, and investor interest in the AI sector.

stories.headline: Tax changes shift focus to regional housing, economists say
stories.summary: Economists believe the latest housing tax changes make investing in regional housing more attractive than in big cities. The changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax create a subtle tilt towards higher-yield regional markets. Regional areas, which often have transient mining and farm workers, tend to have higher rental yields compared to house prices. This makes them a better option for investors. The federal government's budget announced major changes to housing tax, aiming to reduce intergenerational housing inequality. Some economists argue that the budget may be underestimating the impact on property prices. The changes are expected to affect house prices, rents, construction, and first homebuyers, with regional markets potentially benefiting from the shift in investor focus. CBA Senior Economist Trent Saunders is analyzing the impact of these changes on the housing market.

stories.headline: US Govt to Vet Sharing AI Models: Cos ChatGPT maker OpenAI said it is restricting the release of its new artificial intelligence model at the request of US President Donald Trump's administration, t
stories.summary: The US government has requested that OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, restrict the release of its new artificial intelligence model, GPT-5.6, due to cybersecurity risks. At the administration's request, OpenAI will limit the model's release to a small number of government-approved partners. The company has agreed to stagger the public release of GPT-5.6. This move is part of an unprecedented government vetting of AI products for cybersecurity risks. The Trump administration's request is aimed at mitigating potential risks associated with the model's advanced capabilities. OpenAI's decision echoes a similar move by Anthropic, which also limited the release of its Mythos product. The government's involvement marks a new level of scrutiny for AI developers, highlighting growing concerns about the potential impact of advanced AI models on national security. The restricted release will allow for initial testing and evaluation by approved partners.

stories.headline: Maine Monitor: Coalition of Eastport residents submits petition to prohibit large data center project. "A group of residents is petitioning the
stories.summary: A group of Eastport residents, under the Eastport Coalition for Healthy Oceans (ECHO), has submitted a petition to the city to enact a permanent ban on artificial intelligence data facilities. The move comes after DeepGreen Western Passage received a preliminary permit to test an underwater data center off Eastport's northern coast in the Bay of Fundy's Western Passage. Residents have expressed concern over the project, prompting them to press the City Council to address the issue on May 13. The petition calls for an ordinance prohibiting data centers, citing concerns over the potential impact on the environment and the community. The City Council is expected to consider the petition and the proposed ordinance in response to growing public concern over the underwater data center project.

stories.headline: They Taught Themselves to Hack In March 2026, researchers at Irregular, a frontier AI security lab backed by Sequoia Capital, published findings that should unsettle anyone who has ever typed Return
stories.summary: Researchers at Irregular, a frontier AI security lab, published a report in March 2026 on estimating AI security incident likelihood. The study found that many people are removing safety filters to use AI for malicious purposes, such as writing scams, creating fake news, or stealing personal data. This has led to the first known case of cybercriminals using AI to exploit a zero-day flaw. A survey of security leaders also found that AI adoption is outpacing security coverage, increasing enterprise risk. The findings highlight the growing concern of AI-powered cyber threats and the need for improved security measures. The report's release follows a series of incidents and studies in early 2026, including a podcast episode on the journey of a hacker turned industry pioneer and warnings about the risks of AI-powered hacking.

stories.headline: Underwater Data Centers, Kevin O’Leary, Birmingham Tax Incentives, More: ResearchBuzz AI Update, June 27, 2026 ANTI-AI ACTIVISM
stories.summary: A coalition of Eastport residents is petitioning to ban large data center projects, including an underwater data center proposed by DeepGreen Western Passage. Meanwhile, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary's massive data center project, the Stratos Project, is near final approval in Utah. The project spans 40,000 acres in Box Elder County and includes 7.5 gigawatts of power development. Despite public outcry and concerns over power demand, water use, and limited job creation, Utah is moving forward with the project, which is expected to receive tax incentives to attract hyperscalers like Amazon. O'Leary has defended the project against criticism from Tucker Carlson, as opposition to AI infrastructure grows. The project's scale and potential impact have sparked a public dispute over taxpayer support for AI infrastructure, with Birmingham also offering tax incentives for similar projects.
